title: Measure: what does a fixed point cost?

questions.prompt: The tolerance shrank ten-thousand-fold between your first and last bar, yet the calls only about tripled. Why?

choices.why: It keeps only the latest guess; every step is a fresh call to f.

choices.text: Each call shrinks the gap by a steady factor
choices.why: So every further factor of ten in accuracy costs about the same handful of extra calls.

choices.text: Python evaluates cos in constant time
choices.why: True, but the bars count calls, not seconds, so the speed of one call cannot explain them.

checklist.step: Count the calls that really happen, on any search

hints: You can watch calls to a function by handing over a different function that makes a note and then passes the work on.
fixed_point only ever sees the function you give it; it cannot tell f from a stand-in that behaves the same.
Inside measure define a function that adds one to a counter and returns f(x). Pass that to fixed_point, and return its answer together with the counter.
